You Won’t Beat These Levels

The goal is simple: land the shot in the bin. But every level will make you miss again and again.

One Hit Isn’t Enough

The timer is already running. Beat the level faster than anyone else and set a world record.

Too Easy?

Build your own level, beat it twice, and challenge everyone else.

Critical workload overload awakens something in people.

"Never do today what you can put off till tomorrow!"

VTubers who live by that creed have their backs against the wall, and today they plunge into scheduling hell once again.

☆Overview☆

Allocate your resources wisely and survive the one week until the deadline.

A last-minute, task-crunching roguelite! Featuring 3 VTubers and 5 Tasks (a New Merch Plan, an Anniversary Live, and more……).

Mock exams are coming up, but you don't want to study…… The meeting's about to start, but you can't stop yawning.

You can binge short videos all day, yet you can't bring yourself to touch your work.

Sound familiar?

Slacking off is already factored in—so go ahead and build your VTubers' schedules.

……That said, streamers are the ultimate B2C business, so never forget to take care of the fans.

Alas. Caught between the company and the listeners, yet again today.

☆System☆

Make it through each day of the week by building schedules and stockpiling ideas (deckbuilding). Each day is scored by Fulfillment.

There are three resources.

Condition: The stamina your Actions need. Run out and it's game over.

Deck: Your deck of Actions. Deadline day and the days before it demand a lot, so if it runs dry, you can't earn Fulfillment.

Motivation: The currency for growing your Action cards and your VTubers.

In each Scheduling, you place Actions to fit each Time Slot and the Requests coming at you from all sides.

How the game feels changes a lot depending on which VTuber you play.

You can also skip Scheduling to edit your deck or add cards.

But your starting deck is fixed for each run, so you'll need to build a deck that fits each run as it unfolds.

Your deck and VTuber abilities reset with each week you play.

Earn Hustle Boosts (meta-progression) on every run, grow tougher, and take on the Tasks again!!

Age 22

Favorite Drink: Red Bull vodka, kalimotxo

Lifeblood: Feels like she's serving society when she throws away receipts left sticking out of convenience store registers.

Age 22

Can't Stand: Days off lost to "Top 5 Moments When…" vertical videos; the #ArtistsLetsConnect hashtag

Favorite Trope: The cool one who quietly gets serious when their partner gets wrecked

・Aika Yukine

Age 21

Favorite Drink: Barley shochu

Mock Exam Scores (Senior Spring): JP 52.2 Math 60.1 Eng 62.1 Phys 51.0 Chem 58.4

Worries: That keeping her chat in line might make people think she's stuck-up

Loves: Sweets of all kinds

☆Finally☆

Only you, the players, can free them from their limits!

Why they chose this job, and why they hit their limits every day, will be revealed in the main game.

If you're interested, please add it to your Wishlist!

Cruzado is a hand-painted bullet hell roguelite about one crusader's march from Antioch to Jerusalem.

By day, survive the horde: weave through arrows, knives and Greek fire, aim your crossbow by hand and dash through every blow that would kill you. By night, make camp and decide how to spend the few hours before dawn: tend your wounds, forge new gear, draw a card of fate, win a heart... or roll the die and pray nobody finds your fire.

Every choice at camp has a price.


Cruzado is not a pilgrimage for the faint of heart. It is a punishing roguelite, and it expects you to fall.

Arrows, knives, fire pots and charging battering rams fill the screen. Bosses bury the arena in blades and flames, and one careless step can end a run you spent hours building. Your wounds don't heal on their own: whatever you carry out of today's battle, you carry into tomorrow's.

Learn every telegraph. Dash through the storm. Die, and march again.

The road to Jerusalem is paved with fallen crusaders. How far will your faith carry you?


Move freely, aim by hand and dash through danger. Every strong attack is telegraphed: read it and dash at the right moment, because simply walking away won't save you.

  • A new foe every day. 26 enemy types join the fight one battle at a time: lancers and shield bearers, knife throwers and desert hounds, Greek fire throwers, a wandering flute player who charms snakes, laughing hyenas, spitting camels, burrowing scorpions, battering-ram crews, a pigeon keeper who calls for reinforcements... and some very angry geese.
  • Elite champions storm the battlefield on the 5th, 15th and 25th day.
  • There is no running. The sun sinks as the battle drags on, and the day only ends when the last enemy falls.


Three acts. Thirty days. One road.

March from the green hills of the Syrian coast, across the scorched inland desert, to the very walls of Jerusalem. Every act brings new lands, new enemies and a boss waiting at the end of the road, and every step closer to the Holy City is harder than the last.


Every act ends with a boss, and fate decides which one is waiting for you. Nine bosses, three per act, each with its own tricks and a deadlier second phase:

  • Act I: the Iron Emir, the Sultan's Falconer and the Anchor of Tripoli.
  • Act II: the Mamluk Brothers, the Atabeg's Lion and the King of the Desert Raiders.
  • Act III: the Greek Fire Master, the Vizier and his Doubles, and the Lord of the Tower of David.

Learn their patterns, or they will end your crusade.


Your action points are few. Sleep to recover, upgrade your gear, shop, brew or give a gift. You cannot do it all.

Sleeping heals you, but it costs time you could spend growing stronger. Every third night, a visitor comes to your fire:

  • The Blacksmith forges your scrap into upgrades for eight pieces of gear, from boots and crossbow to backpack and sleeping bag.
  • The Alchemist sells potions, then upgrades and refills them, all the way up to level 5.
  • The Merchant sells artifacts and gifts. Search for new offers, or lock the ones you want until her next visit.


Camp alone and the night rolls a d20. Roll low and your camp is ambushed in the dark, where you can only hear them coming. A natural 1 leaves your fire in embers. A natural 20 grants a peaceful night and a deeper sleep.

Light is your greatest ally. Torches and lanterns push back the darkness, and any enemy careless enough to step into your campfire will regret it.


After every battle, choose one of three tarot cards. Its blessing stays with you for the rest of the run, and copies stack.

44 hand-painted cards across four rarities, from small boons to run-defining legends: the Fool shows you more cards, the Archangel saves you from a fatal blow, the Crown of Thorns makes every critical hit bleed. Defeat elites and bosses for a chance at the rarest ones.


Combine 84 artifacts, 20 upgradable potions, 44 tarot cards and eight pieces of gear. Make your bolts bleed, burn, poison or freeze. Chain critical hits, bury the battlefield in bolts, or become a nearly unbreakable wall of armor and faith.

Your backpack is small and your artifact slots are limited. Choose what truly serves your build, and leave the rest behind.

Gold, gems and scrap are scarce. Spend too much today and you may not be ready for tomorrow. Save too much and there may be no tomorrow.


There is more to life than war. Bring gifts, share the fire and slowly win the heart of the Blacksmith, the Alchemist or the Merchant.

A deeper bond unlocks new campfire scenes, discounts and bonuses tied to her craft. But every coin spent on a gift is a coin not spent on steel. Is tomorrow's advantage worth today's sacrifice?

Or stay a lone wolf. The road to Jerusalem is long either way.


Cruzado looks like an illuminated manuscript come to life. Every battle is fought on the pages of an open book, by candlelight, in gouache and ink, while painted cutscenes tell the story like pages of an old chronicle.

A grizzled narrator follows your march, cheering your best shots and warning you when death comes close. Brutal battles and quiet nights by the fire, dark moments and plenty of humor. English voice-over, with subtitles in 13 languages.


  • A punishing top-down bullet hell: aim by hand, read the telegraphs and dash through the storm, or die trying.
  • A day-and-night loop: survive the horde, then make the hard choices at camp with very few action points.
  • A 3-act, 30-day campaign from Antioch to Jerusalem.
  • 26 enemy types, 3 elite champions and 9 bosses chosen by fate.
  • 44 tarot cards that reshape every run.
  • 84 artifacts, 20 upgradable potions and 8 pieces of gear.
  • Bleed, burn, poison, freeze and critical-hit builds.
  • Night ambushes decided by a d20, where light means survival.
  • Friendship and romance that unlock scenes, discounts and bonuses.
  • A hand-painted medieval chronicle with a narrator who talks to you.
  • 53 Steam achievements, from your first boss to the walls of Jerusalem.


Jerusalem waits at the end of a long and merciless road. Will you reach its walls?

Cruzado is our first game, made with a lot of love by a small independent studio. 10% of our profits go to charity.

CrystalCanvas is a puzzle game where three-dimensional artwork takes shape from a rich variety of blocks.

There is nothing complicated to work out.

Just soft jazz, and the gentle pop of each block falling into place.

Settle into a quiet room and watch your piece slowly come together.

Build whatever you like

A Sandbox mode lets you create freely, with no puzzle to follow - and no limit on how much you build.

Design one-of-a-kind 3D art across a variety of spaces, from a living room to a cafe.

Anything you build can be turned into a puzzle and played.

Steam Workshop support

Puzzles you have made and solved yourself can be published to the Steam Workshop.

You can also download and play puzzles made by players around the world.

The library of puzzles to play keeps growing.

Note: the Steam Workshop is a full version feature and is not available in the demo. Anything you build in the demo's Sandbox carries over to the full version, so you can start creating now.

Capture your work beautifully

A full-featured screenshot mode helps you photograph your finished pieces at their best.

Adjust depth of field, saturation, contrast and more to compose your own shot - like photographing a tiny diorama.

About the demo

The demo lets you try a selection of Color by Number stages along with the Sandbox mode.

Your creations and save data carry over to the full version.

Streaming, video uploads, and screenshot posts are all welcome, whether monetized or not.

Fill it. Admire it. Build it. Shoot it.

Step into the world of three-dimensional art with CrystalCanvas.

Crystalase is a relaxing puzzle game. Players assemble beautiful images made entirely of sparkling crystals. Each level involves placing crystal pieces in the correct positions to gradually reveal intricate, colourful artwork.

Unlock new images, explore different themes, and enjoy the rewarding process of turning scattered crystals into dazzling masterpieces.

Crystalase is perfect for puzzle lovers and anyone who enjoys creativity, focus and a touch of sparkle.

✨Go has never been… so accessible with its “tentacles”

This is a game that combines Cthulhu elements with traditional Go.

The game is no longer boring—you’re not just playing Go; you’re competing against a stubborn Cthulhu.

🐙 Playing against Cthulhu

Cthulhu uses its tentacles to grab stones from the void—this eerie style makes every game feel like a ritual.

At some point, Lord Cthulhu removed his right brain and installed the most powerful Go AI on Earth—KataGo.

  • Powerful Go AI: Supports real-time analysis, win rate prediction, and coaching.

  • 5–19-square free board: You can use boards of different sizes to unlock faster, more intense matches.

  • 6 levels of difficulty: Whether you’re a beginner with no experience in Go or a seasoned player, Cthulhu will be a strong opponent.

🍡 Stones stick together

The softest feature in the world of Go—stones formsticky connections with each other. Stones at adjacent, diagonal, or knight’s move positions exhibit different types of connections.

Each stone has its own “expression”.

  • You can interact with the stones; they have life.

  • When a stone has barely any liberties left, it shows “tension”.

  • When you atari a opponent’s stone, it shows “confidence”.

This is actually a clever and compassionate idea from Cthulhu. By observing the expressions, you can understand the situation.

😈 You can definitely get started with Go

The game offers complete teaching and practice materials, and future plans include a “Creative Workshop” where you can freely import question banks.

As long as you follow the complete teaching process by Kusuro and practice regularly with question banks, getting started with Go will be easy.

  • More than a dozen exclusive textbooks: These include basic Go knowledge that beginners need to understand, such as eyes, ladders, points, openings, net attacks, snapbacks, etc.

  • Over a thousand Life and Death Problems: Specialized exercises and practice questions for different types of games.

  • Valuable ancient Go books: You can draw from blind boxes to obtain real ancient Go texts and see the great moves of past players.

  • Collectible term cards: You can gather beautiful Go term cards.

🎵 Drawing a blind box

When playing, remember to throw your captures into the hot pot—Cthulhu insists you remember this.

Then you can draw a blind box and receive Cthulhu’s rewards, including: chess books, term cards, vinyl records, and… stockings!

You can even dress the tentacles in different styles of stockings, and you can even touch the tentacles and adjust the length of the stockings.

“Hmph, if this makes you interested in playing chess, I can wear anything…”

🎮 Future development plans

Current features:

Human-machine match: Competing with KataGo-driven Kukuru

Local matches: Playing against friends face to face on the screen

Teaching: Complete beginner’s lessons in Go

Books: Practice exercises to improve specific skills through training

Emerging features:

Multi-player: Invite Steam friends to play together

Creative workshop: Free creation of Go-related content

At first glance it is Minesweeper, and it wants you to think so. The same flags, the same numbers, the same clean logic, now wrapped onto a three-dimensional solid. Then the board turns, and a clue reaches around a corner to a tile you could not see, and you realize the game you mastered decades ago has rules it never could in two dimensions. Deceptively familiar. Challenging in ways the flat grid cannot be.

Read the whole solid

The numbers sit on the faces of a solid object, not a flat grid. A tile's neighbors can be around a corner, over an edge, or through a tunnel bored into the shape, so you rotate and zoom the board to hold the whole structure in your head before you commit. Reading a solid is a genuine skill, and it is one classic Minesweeper never demanded. When you are not sure what a tile touches, hold Ctrl and right-click it: an outline appears around every neighbor it has, over every edge and through every tunnel, and it stays put while you turn the board.

Really? Another Minesweeper?

Yes, and here is the tell, for anyone who knows the game cold: on a flat grid a tile touches at most eight others. Fold the board into a solid and that ceiling breaks. Across an edge, around a corner, or through a tunnel, a single face can border more than eight neighbors at once, so a 9 is not only possible, it is real, and solving one gets its own achievement. More adjacency means more constraints, more deductions, more brain twisters beyond the flat grid. If you have solved every pattern the old game had, this is where it stops being the old game.

No guessing.

The category's oldest insult is the 50/50: the board that forces you to flip a coin and calls it your fault when you lose. Cube Sweeper never does this. Every board is certified solvable by pure logic, every mine and every hidden gem. When you lose, it is because you missed something, and you will know exactly what. Your skill is the only variable. That is the respect a serious puzzle owes you.

No undo. Mistakes count.

There is no undo, and that is deliberate. A game where you can walk back every wrong step is not testing anything. Here your reading has to be right the first time, and a mistake is real. It is also never random: because the board is always solvable, every loss is a lesson you can name and a board you can play again from the start. For a deeper test, Expedition mode lets the gems you recover become Lifelines, earned protection that absorbs a single mine hit. You are given tools, never a safety rail.

The climb to Expert

Four tiers scale the shape and the difficulty, not just the size, from a small clean board to a dense Expert solid whose folds and tunnels produce the hardest reading in the game. Expert is the summit, and it is a real one: its own developer lost many Expert boards before winning a single one. Three modes let you choose your challenge: Classic for the pure sweep, Gem hunt to deduce and dig for hidden gems, Expedition for the deepest mix of both. Every mode is open at every tier from the first click.

Key features

  • Minesweeper in three dimensions, read across faces, around corners, and through tunnels

  • A certified no-guess guarantee: every mine and every gem yields to pure logic

  • Real difficulty across four tiers, up to an Expert summit its own developer lost many times before winning

  • Three modes (Classic, Gem hunt, Expedition), all open at every tier

  • A second deduction layer: read the clues, dig out hidden gems, a mechanic no other sweeper has

  • A new board every day with streaks, precise times, and per-tier best times to chase

  • Board codes to hand a rival the exact board you played and dare them to beat your time

  • Custom boards: dial the size, carving, mine density, and gems, then share any board as a code

  • A 25-chapter Learning Journey that is the tutorial, tips & tricks, and manual in one

  • 24 achievements, from "Leave No Gem Behind" to "The Hurt Lockerer", including one nobody should ever earn: "The Impossible Made Unlikely"

A new board, forever

This is not a fixed set of levels you finish and shelve. Every generated board is fresh and certified fair, the daily resets every day, and the boards you build are yours to keep and share. Handcrafted, named boards sit alongside the generated ones when you want a designed challenge. You will not run out.

It teaches you to see

Twenty-five hands-on chapters take you from your first click to reading whole solids, one real board per idea. The final part is a strategy guide you can play: the 1-2-1 and the rest of the classic pattern canon, taught flat and then bent over an edge. Ask for a hint and it shows you a move that can be proven, and leaves the clicking to you. It sharpens your reading; it never plays for you.

Cube Sweeper is actively supported after launch. Every board is fair, every board is solvable, and there is always a harder one waiting.

Short Description

A cubic spaceship has crashed on a distant planet. Gather blocks from the world around you, rebuild your ship with them, deliver cargo back to base, and use it to build your tower higher and higher — until you can finally escape the planet.

About the Game

Build your ship from colored blocks, launch it into a dangerous world, and try to bring back as much material as possible. Every block you deliver becomes part of a growing tower, while your progress unlocks new ship capabilities and new ways to deal with the world around you.

But every new flight demands more decisions.

Moving a Single Block Can Change the Entire Ship

A block’s color and position determine what it does as part of the hull. Move just a few cubes, and the ship’s stats, shape, and capabilities can change completely. To reach valuable finds, you may have to rebuild your ship on the fly.

Flying Is About Making Decisions

What should you pick up? What should you leave behind? Is it worth going farther, or is it time to head back? Should you intervene now, or save your resources for later?

Manual actions consume a limited resource, so you cannot endlessly fix every problem. Eventually, you will unlock an autopilot that can take over some of the work, but its capabilities are limited too — and its decisions still come at a cost.

Your Ship Evolves Alongside You

As you progress, you unlock new abilities, upgrades, and ways to interact with your ship. They do not replace its construction: you still need to build a solid hull yourself. How you use these new possibilities depends on the ship you have built and the situation during each individual flight.

The World Follows Clear Rules

The higher your tower grows, the more dangerous your flights become. Different hazards force you to rethink your usual tactics and ship designs. When you encounter a new hazard, you can learn its rules and prepare better the next time.

Features

  • Build your ship from colored blocks whose properties depend on their position;

  • Rebuild and reshape your ship during flight;

  • Decide which blocks you find should become part of the ship;

  • Spend a limited resource to intervene in your ship’s operation;

  • Unlock new abilities, upgrades, and autopilot as you progress;

  • Adapt your ship design and tactics to changing hazards;

  • Move closer to your goal with every successful flight.

Cubic Color Confusion is a grid-based puzzle game with a unique color-based mechanic where every move changes the puzzle you're trying to solve.

Collect valuable artefacts, adapt to new challenges, and master a complex ruleset built around color cycling, spatial awareness, and strategic planning.

Different cube types, changing terrain, elevation, locks, keys, and other puzzle elements will constantly challenge your understanding of the world and its rules.

Core Gameplay

Create Paths

Every move changes the color of the tile you enter and directly affects the available options to solve the puzzle.
Cubes can only travel across neutral tiles and tiles matching their own color. Use the color-cycle mechanic to open new routes and solve seemingly impossible puzzles. Plan carefully to create possibilities without locking yourself in before reaching every artefact.

Cubic Cooperation

Let your cubes work together in surprising ways to overcome challenges no single cube could solve alone.

Features

  • Handcrafted Puzzles: Over 100 carefully designed levels.

  • Dynamic Core Mechanic: A unique color-based rule system where every move changes the environment.

  • Multiple Cube Types: Control different cubes with distinct movement abilities and behaviors.

  • Varied Layouts: Master elevation differences, locks and keys, cube recoloring, fragile terrain, and other puzzle elements.

  • Operator Feed: Unlock entries containing Corporate messages, rule explanations, and Employee logs.

  • Integrated Level Editor: Create, share, and play custom puzzles through Steam Workshop support.

Can you master every challenge and become Hullet Corporation's most valuable Operator?

Roguelike-inspired builds. Long-term idle cultivation.

Fire extra projectiles, pierce and chain through enemies, or pull them together and finish with on-kill explosions — Arcana talents and gear effects give the same skill different ways to fight. Recruit companions for a five-hero squad, combine techniques and talents, and hunt gear that brings your team's synergies to life. Battles are automatic; the build is yours.

Change Your Skills with Arcana


Add projectiles and piercing, expand areas, extend effects, or trigger another cast with Echo. Gain ten types of Arcana through the fifth talent tier and random gear effects, then combine them to shape how compatible skills fight.

Five Heroes. Your Synergy.


Build a five-hero party from 25 classes, combining skills, techniques and talents. One hero sets enemies ablaze while another consumes the flames to empower strikes; certain healer talents can reset an ally's tactic cooldown. Choose teammates and gear around these interactions to build distinct playstyles from the same five slots.

Find the Gear Your Build Needs


Collect gear, materials and cultivation techniques from the horde; keep what fits your build and sell or salvage the rest. Refine your equipment through crafting, tempering, enchanting and reforging. Tempering stays with the item when you pass it to another hero, and matching gems unlock set bonuses.

Make Your Next Breakthrough Count


Brew pills to build cultivation, face inner-demon trials as you advance, and survive heavenly tribulations at major breakthroughs. After a major breakthrough, choose one of three realm traits to strengthen your hero and further shape your build. Forge an artifact to give a hero an additional skill with its own cooldown.

Beyond the Nine Regions


Challenge nine regions with 250 floors each, testing your party and gear against different monsters and bosses. Advance deep into the ninth region to unlock the Endless Abyss and the Primordial Secret Realm, then keep hunting loot, growing your heroes and pushing your team's limits. Between pushes, run your town and send ships out to sea.

Progress at Your Own Pace


Buy once, play solo — no dailies, no log-in rewards, no seasons, no microtransactions, no ads. Auto-potions, auto-advance, auto-sell and 1x/2x battle speed. Earn up to 24 hours of offline EXP and coins, then come back and plan your next push.

Bring your demo save into Early Access to continue growing your squad and explore expanded systems and content.

Roadmap


Throughout Early Access, we will prioritize fixes for player-reported issues, performance improvements and balance adjustments, while gradually expanding the game with:

- A second cycle and harder challenges: Take your existing squad and accumulated progress into tougher regions, face stronger enemies and pursue higher-tier gear.
- Five new classes: New recruits will bring fresh skills and synergies to your five-hero squad.
- Spirit pets: Raise a pet that fights alongside your squad, feed it spirit fruit and evolve it to unlock new forms and combat abilities.
- Battle formations: Choose formations around your squad's skills and build to explore new team synergies.
- Realm trials: Face distinctive foes that put your squad's damage, survival and teamwork to the test.
- Equipment sets: Collect sets designed around different builds and combine them with techniques, talents and Arcana to discover new ways to fight.
- Cultivation abode: Build and manage your own cultivation retreat, adding new goals to your long-term progression.

These are our current development plans, listed without a fixed release order. Details and priorities may change with development progress and player feedback. We will share progress through Steam announcements and Discord.

So, here's the deal: a global conspiracy weaponized social media and turned (almost) everyone into a mindless NPC. Yes, those kinds of NPCs. The ones repeating the same terrible dialogue loops, trends, and opinions.

The vibes are... terrible.

You command the last free-thinkers: an "elite" (questionable) resistance force of Chads. Your impossible mission? Get everyone to log off.

But beating the horde isn't about clicking on the nearest idiot until they fall over.

Every turn is a tactical puzzle.

Study the grid. Work out how enemies will react. Push one NPC into another. Line up a shot. Use the environment. Protect your Jammers. Chain your squad's abilities together and try to find the move that turns a complete disaster into a beautifully stupid masterplan.

And if your beautifully stupid masterplan turns out to just be stupid?

Rewind.

Undo your moves, try a different approach and experiment until you crack the problem. Finding the solution is half the fun - whether it's an elegant five-move sequence or something involving three Chads, a baseball bat and an extremely unfortunate NPC.

Build your squad, discover new tactical tools and fight your way through 45 handcrafted levels to the Facepalm Tower (yes, really) and save humanity from itself.

Key Features:

  • Every Level Is a Tactical Puzzle: Take your time, study the board and figure out how to turn a bad situation into the perfect sequence of moves. Positioning, enemy behaviour, abilities, and the environment can all become part of your solution.

  • Protect the Jammers: Those civilian Jammers are the only things stopping the horde from posting more cringe. Keep them safe. Please. (Friendly fire is not friendly).

  • Think Real Hard (Turn-Based): No rush. Stare at the grid. Analyze the NPCs. Have a snack. Then execute your flawless 5D chess move.

  • The "Tactical Oopsie" Button: Accidentally walk into a mob? Shoot your best, Chad, in the back? Hit rewind, pretend it never happened, and try something that isn't that.

  • Assemble Some Guys: Find powerful new gear (like a really nice bat) and recruit 11 unique Chads. They all have distinct abilities and, presumably, very strong opinions on pineapple pizza.

  • Make Your Chads Slightly Less Bad: Level 'em up, hone their special skills, and maybe they'll stop missing shots. (No promises).

  • A Truly Alarming Amount of Weapons: Seriously, who left over 20 different guns and blunt objects lying around? Well, finders keepers.

  • Fight 30+ Flavors of "Ugh": Adapt your tactics to overcome a diverse horde of over 30 different enemy types, from the 'Well, Actually' foot-soldier to 8 powerful bosses. They're all very cross.

  • Achieve Online Validation: Prove you're the real tactical genius by getting your name at the top of the leaderboards. Go on. You've earned it.

  • A 45-Level Headache: Fight your way across a corrupted Zoo (the animals are fine, just very opinionated) Museum, and more all to reach the final confrontation at the... Facepalm Tower..

Step into the shoes of an antique shop owner living a dangerous double life. By day, manage your store, appraise rare items, trade with customers, and keep your business afloat. By night, descend beneath the surface into secret tunnels to unearth hidden relics, dig through the dark, and deal with the underworld’s dangerous demands.

KEY FEATURES:

  •  Run Your Antique Shop: Buy, inspect, restore, and sell unique historical items to customers during the daylight hours.

  •  Dig Into the Underground: Grab your shovel and bucket to excavate mystery-filled tunnels and uncover rare antiquities beneath the city.

  • Physics & Tool Interactions: Use real-time physical tools to dig, transport dirt, and manage your inventory on the fly.

  •  High-Stakes Double Life: Balance legitimate business profits with the risky demands of the mafia syndicate waiting in the shadows.

  •  Atmospheric Mystery: Unravel the dark secrets of the town as you dig deeper and expand your operations.

Work the Night Shift

Cursed Gas Station is a first-person psychological horror game set in the 1990s. Cole starts a night shift at an isolated gas station. The station's owner offers him a job and a room to stay in. For Cole, it seems like the opportunity he needs to get his life back on track.

Work the register, fuel cars, restock the shelves, and keep the station clean. Talk to the people who stop by and get to know the station and its surroundings.

When the Routine Breaks

As the nights go on, this routine becomes increasingly unsettling. A strange conversation can turn into an argument. Small details you notice around the station begin to make you question what you know about the place. As strange sounds and unexplained events pile up, you start to wonder whether the building where you work and sleep is safe.

Over Several Nights

Try to make sense of what is happening at the station while carrying on with your work. Each shift leaves you with a new question about the station's past and the people around you.

Discover how the events at the station unfold over several nights.

Features

  • A first-person psychological horror experience.

  • Everyday gas station tasks, from working the register and fueling cars to restocking shelves and cleaning.

  • Conversations with customers and unsettling encounters.

  • An atmospheric horror story unfolding over several nights.

  • Multiple endings.

The yard is under attack. The cats were napping there.

The pests have arrived. They’re adorable. They’re completely out of line.

Cute Kitty WAR is an arena survival game about defending a backyard with an increasingly unreasonable collection of weapons. Fight through 12 waves, turn your haul into a powerful build, and hold the fence against a neighborhood’s worth of trouble.

The cats would like their yard back.

Local co-op for up to 4 on one PC – no controller required. Players share keyboards (four key layouts: WASD, Arrows, IJKL, TFGH – a second keyboard helps a big group) or use controllers, in any mix.

Find your favorite cat. Discover your next ridiculous build.

Choose from 48 playable cats, each with distinct abilities, starting gear, and a journey to complete. Become a bruiser, build a gunner’s arsenal, or put a gardener in charge of an expanding network of defenses.

Between waves, shop for combinations that bring your strategy to life. With 97 weapons across 17 classes and 194 items, there’s room to experiment with pets, pacts, curious equipment, and a deeply questionable amount of luck.

Which purchase will pull your build together? Which cat will you try next?

Bring the whole neighborhood watch.

Play solo or gather up to four players for couch co-op. Pick your cats, build your arsenals, and face the invasion together. Co-op offers a more forgiving challenge, giving friends and family room to join the defense.

There are enough pests for everyone.

Weather the storm. Learn the enemy.

Face 143+ creatures, including 10 bosses, while storms transform the yard around you. Rain sweeps across the grass, wind carries trouble, lightning strikes, and ponds flood through five escalating weather levels.

Learn attack patterns, watch for warnings, and find your way through the mayhem. Ready for a tougher watch? Climb six danger levels, with twin bosses waiting at Danger 5.

Record your discoveries and fill the trophy wall in Kittain’s Log. The yard has quite a few residents worth remembering.

The fence is only the beginning.

Survive all 12 waves to unlock an endless mode where the yard’s folklore comes calling. Set the pace as its creatures arrive, from the weakest to the strongest, and discover how far your build can take you.

Something waits at the end of that procession.

We’ll let it introduce itself.

In a kingdom consumed by rust, three unlikely heroes—armed only with kitchen utensils—must battle their way through a decaying world to restore light and beauty.

Players explore three vast regions, solving puzzles, discovering new abilities, and battling enemies in a strategic turn-based system where combining attacks unlocks powerful synergies.

✅ Combo-Based Combat: Master a rhythm-driven attack chaining system where timing is key to maximizing damage.

✅ Exploration-Based Progression: No grinding or leveling—unlock abilities by discovering secrets in the world.

✅ Reactive NPCs & Story: Your choices affect quests, NPC behavior, and the world’s state.

✅ A Unique Fantasy World: Inspired by Paper Mario, Hollow Knight, and Studio Ghibli’s aesthetic.

Every route is live. Your torch fuel is sealed.


Cutset is a logic puzzle about shutting down industrial pipe networks. Cut a pipe or close a valve, then account for every route from source to sink. Thick material takes more fuel; steel pipe cannot be cut.

The ration is exact. Each level has one unique, provably optimal shutoff, calculated before it ever reaches the game, and your torch carries exactly enough fuel to match it. There is no partial credit. Your plan is optimal, or the water still runs.

That is where the pressure comes from. A route can look promising while its total cost still refuses to close. You may have the idea and still not finish the arithmetic. Every operation asks the same question: does this use of fuel stop enough routes to justify it?

There are 80 levels in all. After seven compact introductions, the networks grow from 8 junctions to as many as 40. Valves, uncuttable steel, and multiple sources and sinks keep changing what an efficient shutoff looks like. Nine Steam achievements mark precise first cuts and mixed pipe-and-valve work. The last one is simply for clearing all eighty.

The interface uses a crisp industrial-instrument style and supports 11 languages.

One-time purchase. No in-app purchases. No ads. No internet required.

Cyan Moon is a sandbox built around procedurally generated patterns and growth.

Create your own patterns with the extensive settings menu. Want bigger and faster simulations? Just change the corresponding settings and restart the simulation (if needed). 
You can make small changes to the simulation parameters and get big changes to the outcome.
The game comes with presets and you can easily save your own custom ones. Share your presets with a Share Code that everyone who has the game can use to import them.
You can save simulations as transparent PNG files to your chosen location.

There is no goal. There is no way to play it correctly. You can only play it your way. And that is the right way.
Play at your own pace and enjoy it.

CyberNeon CoreProtocol is a cyberpunk pixel-art roguelike deck-building game.

Choose a mercenary with unique abilities and venture deep into the city network along procedurally generated infiltration routes. Collect and upgrade cards, install cyberware, and combine combat protocols. Activate Overclock at critical moments to break through machine armies and multi-phase bosses.

Every run presents new routes and encounters. Read enemy intentions, manage your hand and resources, and reach the AI Core before the system erases you.

Official QQ Group : 1109070721

In a cyberpunk underground where the neon never dies, a rogue AI is seizing control of the city network. Corporations have sealed off the truth, machine legions hold the streets, and you — a hired bounty hunter — must fight your way down a dangerous intrusion path into the system core, eliminating every enemy in your way.

But this is not a mission that can be won through brute force.

Build your deck, install lethal cyberware, manage your sync protocols, and make hard choices with every action. Your route, your tactics, and your build will together decide whether you live long enough to reach the final node.

Every run generates a brand-new intrusion map. Choose your route and decide between combat, elite enemies, shops, events, rest stops, and cyberware clinics.

Every node can open up new opportunities — or cut your run short.

Pick the mercenary that fits you and build your tactics around their unique abilities and signature cards.

  • Viktor Kane — The BreacherTrades blows to build Rage and destroys enemies with devastating melee attacks.

  • Maya Novak — The Daemon HandlerPlants viruses in enemies, letting corrosion and system collapse spread over multiple turns.

  • Adrian Cross — The Fire ControlManages ammunition and precision shots, landing consecutive critical hits at the decisive moment.

  • Céline Voss — The InfiltratorUses stealth, phantoms, and rapid strikes to execute enemies before they can react.

As the run progresses, mercenaries earn experience and unlock more exclusive programs, giving each character a sharper growth path.

Earn new cards from combat rewards and events, upgrade existing programs, and gradually forge a deck of your own.

Use attacks, block, buffs, viruses, corrosion, vulnerability, and a range of special effects to find synergies between cards.

Do you chase burst damage, or grind enemies down through defense and sustained damage? Every battle forces you to reassess your hand, your energy, and the enemy's intent.

Build up Sync in combat to activate powerful combat protocols. Combine your deck with your mercenary's abilities, enter an Overclocked state at the right moment, and unleash burst power that can turn the tide.

Overclocking is not free power. Judge when to go all-in and when to hold your resources, so the system doesn't turn on you against the threats ahead.

Acquire a variety of cyberware from black markets, clinics, and boss fights to add lasting effects to your combat system.

Boost card draw, Sync, block, attack, status effects, or resource cycles. Combine cyberware across different body slots to build a combat style that matches your deck.

Every install makes your hunter stronger — and may also make you more reliant on a particular strategy.

From rogue machines and corporate defense systems to eerie digital phantoms, you will fight your way through five escalating zones:

  • Neon Slums

  • Mech Foundry

  • Corporate Labs

  • Cyberspace

  • AI Core

Each chapter features a unique mix of enemies, elite encounters, and a final boss. Bosses shift phases based on their health, changing attack patterns, summoning reinforcements, empowering themselves, and even unleashing a lethal termination protocol.

Read the enemy's intent, crack their attack rhythm, and destroy them before the system wipes you out.

Failure does not mean it's over. Complete battles, defeat bosses, and collect cards and cyberware to unlock new content and progression options that let the next run go further.

Every run leaves behind data.

Every choice changes the outcome.

Jack in. Take the contract. Be the last program still running.

  • Cyberpunk pixel-art Roguelike deck-building game

  • Procedurally generated intrusion maps with a different route every run

  • 4 mercenaries with unique mechanics, signature cards, and Overclocking abilities

  • Turn-based combat with attacks, block, buffs, and a variety of status effects

  • Forge a personalized playstyle through card upgrades and cyberware installs

  • 5 chapters, elite encounters, and multi-phase boss fights

  • Pixel art that blends neon, glitch code, and industrial machinery

  • Cyberpunk music and ambient sound design for an immersive atmosphere

  • Mercenary experience and content unlocks that carry across runs

Outsmart them instead of counting on the whims of the die!

"He was one step from the finish — I froze him, and my partner picked him off."

"He brought out his mighty Tank, and I put a rocket into it, straight onto a mine that sent the big guy back to base."

"I needed a three and nothing else — my partner cast the Underdog's ult and left the number panel to me. Sadly, a rival knocked the Underdog out a step before my win. Why did I forget to raise the shield?! :("

That is what almost every turn looks like here: every move has an answer, and every answer has one of its own.

Before we made this game, we spent years inspired by the classic — and arrived at rules where, on that same classic board, skill really does decide a lot.

Play solo against bots, with friends at one screen, online with cross-play — or mix it all in one match. With a mouse, a gamepad, or a finger on a touchscreen.

The card mode

Plan combinations several turns ahead, so every turn sets up the next one. Run the game with cards instead of letting the die run you.

Everyone plays the same deck: movement cards, action cards (some of them very strong!) and junk cards you'd rather avoid. The card mode has three difficulty levels — they set how much junk clogs the deck, and the Scout class becomes your filter against it, which pays off most at the higher ones.

Hands are open, which is what makes playing at one screen easy — and what lets you "suggest" your rivals' moves worse than the ones they were hoping to find.

The die

It hasn't gone anywhere: three of the rule sets still use it. Two of the four leave the classic untouched — out of respect for it, and for the people who love it. Or for anyone who is simply more comfortable with a die.

The game also settles the old suspicion that haunts every digital dice board game. After each match, it shows a fairness score for the die across three measures: the average roll, how evenly the faces came up, and how long the same-face streaks ran. No "the game is rigging it" — just the numbers.

Classes

The game already has four classes: Tank, Saboteur, Scout and Underdog. Each one carries a passive it always has, and an ult of its own. They are described in detail inside the game, under Rules, on the "Classes & Ults" tab.

If you want, class chips can be added even to the classic rule sets.

Play, counter-play, co-op

Here almost every move has an answer.

  • You can knock out anyone except the Tank. But even the Tank goes back to base if it takes out a Saboteur — the two of them together.

  • An active ult shields the whole team. Knock out the chip that cast it, though, and the shield drops from all the rest.

  • Freeze an enemy chip and it won't move for a turn. Rockets are the answer to that: they thaw your own chips and your partner's.

  • The "Block action cards" card shuts off every enemy action for a turn: no swaps, no teleports, no thawing at the worst possible moment.

Team play

Any rule set can be played every player for themselves, but it is the card mode where team play gives you the most that is new:

  • A rival near the finish and out of your reach? Hit them with a rocket to throw them back closer to your partner, then freeze them on your next move. They will have a hard time getting free on their turn, and your partner can pick off what was out of reach a minute ago.

  • Spent a powerful ult and waiting for its recharge card? Your partner can help, if that card reaches them first ;).

  • Your partner can thaw your chips with their rockets.

  • "Block action cards" shuts off your opponents' actions, but not your partner's — their cards keep working.

  • The Underdog's ult opens a panel for picking a number. Don't use it yourself and it passes to your partner, who picks instead.

Play 2 vs 2 when the pairs are even, or try 2 vs 1 and 2 vs 1 vs 1 when two newcomers take on more experienced players.

Rules you shape

Sometimes you sit down to play and the rules are not the ones you are used to — and it grates. That is why any rule set here can be tuned in detail. Put your favourite rules together once, and play that way from then on.

Even for the classic you can choose what earns an extra move, whether there are safe zones and how many of them, and so on. Want more depth — add classes with passive abilities, ults on top, and set the conditions under which they recharge.

There is even Peaceful mode, so you can play with the youngest in the family, the ones who take it hard when a chip one step from the finish gets knocked back.

Worlds and the people in them

The game already has several atmospheric worlds, and you can play in the setting of any of them. Each world brings its own ambient sounds, music and race.

Races are an animated cosmetic skin for the classic chips: in gameplay terms they give no advantage. More worlds and races are planned.

Mix players however you like

One game can hold online players, hot-seat players and bots together. You can add a hot-seat player to any online seat, and bots come in three difficulty levels. If someone drops for a moment, a bot steps into their seat so nobody waits, and they take it back the moment they return.

Stats and awards

The game counts everything — and shows no less. Successful plays light up right in the match: your first knockout, your first chip at the finish, a knockout on a chip you have just bounced into a rival with a rocket, and plenty more.

After every match a window opens automatically with the highlights for each player: knockouts, losses, rockets, freezes, distance, points...

From the main menu there is a separate window with your all-time stats, gathered across every match you play.

The same window holds the history of the matches you have played.

Save and pick up anywhere

The game auto-saves at the start of every turn, on every player's device at once. So even if the power cuts out for everyone at the same moment, you can restore the match from anyone's auto-save and lose no more than a single turn. Start on one device and finish on several, or the other way around. Didn't finish a game around the table? Pick it back up online by joining the room's save by invitation. And link your own devices together to pull saves between them straight from the cloud.

Demo and full version

What the demo includes:

  • Four rule sets, each one adjustable to your liking.

  • Two of the four chip classes, Tank and Saboteur, in the rule sets with a die. Card matches in the demo are played without classes.

  • Online for two players, with Remote Play Together supported. Text chat included.

  • Bot matches and play at one screen, with no limits.

  • Two save slots, kept on your own computer.

  • English, Ukrainian, German, French.

What the full version adds:

  • All four classes, Tank, Saboteur, Scout and Underdog, card matches included.

  • Online for up to four players, with voice chat.

  • The host can drop out and the match carries on.

  • Match history.

  • Far more save slots, kept in the cloud.

Where this game came from

For me it started back in 2003 — as a student I played one of the digital adaptations of the classic with friends over a beer. Later, when I had children of my own, we played it as a family.

We liked how the game looked and how it sounded, the knockouts most of all. But in time it started to grate that so much of it hung on the die: often you could tell from the start who was going to win.

So I made my own copy, one we could change ourselves. As an experiment we switched an extra move on and off — for a knockout, for a six, for reaching the finish. That is where the idea came from: let any player tune this as easily as we did.

Then came classes with passive abilities — and suddenly the order in which you brought your chips out mattered. Ults followed, and they gave team play a point. That is how D.A.M.N! Dice came to be.

But what players could do still hung on the die: it decided your options, and it left no room to plan ahead or to agree on a plan with your partner.

That is when it became clear this could only be solved by replacing the die with cards, several of which you can play in a single turn. And the arguments along the lines of:

  • of course you won, you drew swaps while I drew turn skips;

  • you kept rolling sixes and I kept rolling ones;

  • is it worth the risk of stepping on a "?" cell…

simply went away. That is how D.A.M.N! Cards was born, and it became the face of our game.

We have been playing it 2 vs 2 as a family for months now and we are not tired of it. The emotions in front of the screen run high enough that one mouse has already been broken trying to stop a winning move. We hope you enjoy it as much as we do ;)!

Step into 1980s Korea for the ultimate retro alleyway chase!


Long before video games, children in 1970s–80s Korea ruled the alleyways with a high-stakes team game of tag called DABANGGU.

Taggers capture runners and hold them at base while the remaining runners fight to stay free. Wait for an opening, reach the base, and shout “Dabanggu!” to pull off a dramatic jailbreak and free your captured teammates.

Disguise yourself as familiar street props such as benches, flowerpots, and garbage bags, or reveal your position with a cheeky whistle to taunt the taggers. Just remember: when the final minute begins, Booster Time makes every tagger faster.

Key Features

  • A Korean team tag game — Experience a tense cycle of chasing, capture, imprisonment, and rescue.
  • Online matches for up to 15 players — Create an alley and split into taggers and runners with friends.
  • Solo play with BOTs — Explore all three alleys with BOT participants when playing alone.
  • Prop disguises and hiding — Blend into the neighborhood and make taggers doubt what they see.
  • Three Korean neighborhoods — Race through Ikseon-dong, Yeonnam-dong, and Bukchon Hanok Village.
  • Match scoring and a Top 5 ranking — Earn points through jailbreaks and daring escapes.
  • Paint your clay character — Create a look of your own with the character customization tools.

A Letter from the Developer


Hello! I am a solo developer and lifelong game fan. I created DABANGGU because I wanted to introduce more people to the alleyway games played by Korean children in the 1970s and 1980s.

There is still room for DABANGGU to grow, and I plan to keep improving its stability and polish. I will also continue exploring future alley maps inspired by the beauty of Korea and places loved by local communities.

If there is an alley or neighborhood from your country that you would love to share, please tell me through the Steam Community or the map-suggestion channel in the official Discord linked on the Game Website. Your suggestions may be considered as inspiration and reference material for future maps.

Thank you for your interest and support!

DATAWANDER is a walking simulator where you wander through a mysterious digital space.

There are no clear objectives such as combat or goals; only the act of walking. Explore a resort-like map, discovering the reactions of action buttons, hidden paths, and fantastical moments.

There are also small mini-games scattered throughout. Explore the virtual world in your free time.

Features:

• Quiet and fantastical digital space

• Minimalist exploration experience

• Multiple mini-games for relaxation

• A game you can enjoy in short bursts

Controls:

WASD or arrow keys: Movement

Mouse: Camera movement

Left Ctrl: Action

Experience modern naval helicopter search and rescue operations.

Fly a naval helicopter on search and rescue missions at sea. Locate people and objects in the open ocean, use the helicopter's search equipment, and recover survivors using the rescue hoist.

Take on the different tasks of a rescue helicopter crew, from flying the aircraft and searching for survivors to handling the recovery. Missions take place in changing weather and visibility conditions, from daylight to darkness and clear skies to severe weather.

Search areas and mission conditions vary, requiring you to locate survivors rather than simply follow a marker to their position. DATUM: Rescue One focuses on the experience of conducting maritime search and rescue operations as a helicopter crew.

DEAD RECALL is a 2D side-scrolling survival action shooter roguelite set amid a modern war being consumed by organisms known as the Aberrants.

AIM. FIRE. SURVIVE.

Take direct control of the machine gun mounted on an armored vehicle carrying an artificial brain. Aim with the mouse and choose every direction and moment of fire yourself—attacks are never automatic. Move, hover, descend rapidly, and reposition to intercept biological threats advancing from the ground and the sky.

EVOLVE YOUR BUILD WITH BIOMASS

Harvest biomass and select Neural Branches. Combine ammunition traits such as homing rounds, armor-piercing rounds, grenades, and ricochets with vehicle upgrades and equipment including the Arm, Slaughter Bumper, and Strong Acid Tank. Each choice reshapes your area control, close-range lethality, and endurance.

A BIOLOGICAL THREAT THAT ESCALATES

Face ordinary Aberrants, Abnormal Specimens born from failed fusion between multiple organisms, and powerful Neural Relay Organisms. Enemy variety and combat pressure intensify as you advance through three distinct sectors.

RECONSTRUCT THE WAR FROM ITS FRAGMENTS

Collect Aberrant Investigation Records and dated documents marked with their discovery locations. Piece together what happened to this world and trace the origin of the weapon consuming it.

FULL VERSION

The full version is planned to feature eight vehicles with distinct handling and combat characteristics, and eight stages. Each stage will introduce its own battlefield theme and unique Aberrants, expanding the range of combat styles, builds, and biological threats.

STEAM DEMO

The planned demo will include the opening cinematic and the complete first stage: progression through three sectors, the build system, Abnormal Specimens, Neural Relay Organisms, and the stage-clear objective.

Game Overview

The protagonist is Yuji Ichinose, a highly educated lawyer. May is a glamorous beauty of French and Japanese descent who committed attempted murder to avenge someone dear to her. Yuji sees that May is so pure-hearted and single-minded that her very sincerity could lead her down a dark path. Determined to protect her, he decides to stand by her side. Eventually, the two marry... Yuji surrounds May with a life of luxury, hoping to help her forget her desire for revenge. Just when he finally believes everything will be all right... May disappears.

All she leaves behind is a handbag found in a hotel restroom and a locked smartphone. Desperate to find her, Yuji begins uncovering the secrets she has kept from him. Messaging apps, social media, and secret direct messages... What he discovers is a shocking side of the wife he believed to be so innocent and modest...

Game System

■ Explore the Smartphone

Freely explore the web browser, messaging apps, social media, password manager, and more. Find passwords to log in to social media accounts, access private DMs, and uncover new information.

■ Expand Your Investigation with Keywords

As you explore, you may discover new "Keywords." Search for them in the browser or on social media to uncover hidden information.

■ Organize Clues and Draw Conclusions

As you gather evidence and information, use the "Deduction" feature to piece together the case. Connect the clues you've collected and uncover the truth behind May's disappearance.

■ Credits

Production & Scenario: Nagi Kurokawa

Character Design & Main Graphics: necomilk

Japanese Logo: Thugu

Voice of May (main game only): Yuki Toyokawa

Special Thanks: BIG OPPAI LOVERS

DELVERS: Dragon's Hoard is a run-based party autobattler incremental. You never control a hero in combat. You recruit them at the campfire, gear them, spend the gold from your last run on a sprawling zodiac skill tree — then send four of them marching into the depths and watch the formation fight without you. Every delver carries their own Vigor bar, healing is strictly rationed, and every depth costs more than the last. When the party falls the run is over — but the gold, the gear and the levels you hauled back are permanent, and they buy a party that reaches further next time.



THE DELVE
Your party walks down depth by depth, and the dark escalates as you go: the Greenfields give way to the Mire, the Wastes, Sporewood, the Catacombs, and finally The Deep. Dozens of kinds of foe hold the road, and past the ordinary ranks stand elites, minibosses and apex foes — hand-built counters that come dressed in the gear meant to beat the class they hunt. Every fight is won or lost by the party you built at the fire, and the end of every run lays the truth out in THE RECKONING — what each hero dealt, took, blocked and healed. When you're farming, arm ⟳ auto-delve and the next run marches itself. Close the game and the road keeps paying a share into your purse while you're away.



THE HOLLOW KEEP
Past the road lies Greymarrow, a cursed city that is the endgame. You climb it district by district — the Lantern Ward, Gallows Row, the Drowned Market, Bonechapel, and the keep at its crown — and after every room you pick one of two or three doors: a back street that calms the city, a guardhouse with better finds, a vault that only opens for the right delver, a lair that hunts one of yours. Dread rises as you climb: the city sends elites, and its hunter joins the fight. Every fifth room ends on a named villain with a weakness a particular class answers, and a clock — silver under forty seconds, gold under twenty-five with every delver still standing. Finds ride in your satchel and are yours only if you leave with them or slay the villain. The city pays what the road cannot: element set pieces that amplify your party's elemental chord, and a weekly writ that changes the rules of the climb for everyone, every week.



THE HOARD
Loot is the spine of the game. Every delver wears eight slots — weapon, offhand, helm, chest, gloves, boots, ring, amulet — and drops climb a ladder: common, magic, rare, legendary, and the mythics you forge yourself. The affix pool runs deep and spans six tiers, and it reads like the dungeon-crawlers it comes from: Jagged, Cruel, Swift, Keen, Brutal and Giantslaying on weapons; of Stone, of Warding, of the Prism, of Fortune, of Greed and of the Leech on everything else. Weapon bases are class-specific — the Lancer's spears, the Berserker's greathammer, the Necromancer's bone scepter, the Alchemist's alembic.



Most of what drops is smart loot, weighted toward the party you actually field, and nothing equips behind your back: the haul rides home in your satchel, THE SPOILS lays it out at camp, upgrades glow green, and one tap dons the best of it. At the top sit the named legendaries — a chase piece for every class, each carrying a power the tree cannot grant. The Drakespur bites back: half of every blow the Lancer blocks returns to the one who swung it. Truefeather makes every fifth arrow a guaranteed headshot. The Moonchalice swells the Lunar Tide and shields the weariest ally with every cast. Feed ten legendaries to THE MYTHIC FORGE and they become one mythic that keeps the anchor's base, its slot and its power — and when a roll on a worn piece is wrong, gold buys another.



THE CAMPFIRE
Everything between runs happens at the fire, under the sky itself — one zodiac sign hangs overhead at a time, and turning the wheel brings the next sign, and the next delver, into view. Strangers walk up out of the dark to be recruited under their own constellation: Lancer, Berserker, Archer, Cleric, Wizard, Thief, Bard, Paladin, Necromancer, Warlock, Druid, Alchemist — each with its own range, cadence and row in the formation. Only four march at once, so the party you take down is a real decision. Each sign belongs to an element, and marching two of a kind wakes a chord that the city's set pieces amplify. The ones who stay by the fire keep what they earned: heroes bank experience permanently, class by class, across Might, Grace, Vigor, Lore, and those levels survive runs and prestige alike.



THE SKY
The skill tree IS the sky: twelve zodiac signs, each a constellation of minor stars, notables and a keystone at its end. Stars reveal themselves as you buy toward them, skills rank up rather than switching on, signs unlock class paths, and fusions exist only where two branches meet. Nothing is locked behind a respec fee — the tree refunds what it reforges, so a build is something you keep rebuilding. The whole game plays with mouse, keyboard or controller alike.



THE LONG NIGHT
Every tenth depth a dragon blocks the road, telegraphing a cone of fire your party has to walk out of; kill it and it drops a Dragon Heart, the currency behind the tree's most dangerous keystones. Clear the ladder and difficulty tiers reopen the whole descent, harder, with better gear waiting at the bottom. When a lifetime of runs stops paying, the Rekindling burns your tale for embers — a permanent currency that buys the back half of the roster and the tree's ember nodes — and you may swear a vow for the era to come, which pays more for playing it the hard way.



WHAT THE FULL GAME ADDS
The free demo is the earlier build of the game, complete and uncapped. The full game is where the road continues:
  • The Hollow Keep — the cursed city of Greymarrow, its villains, its doors, its dread, its medals and the weekly writ
  • Element set pieces that only the city drops, and the party chords they amplify
  • Gold rerolls on a worn piece's affix at the forge
  • Era vows sworn at the Rekindling
  • Gold that keeps coming in while the game is closed
  • Steam achievements and cloud saves
  • New content lands here first

This game is a tactical SRPG with a strong emphasis on strategy and storytelling.

A 2D grid system is embedded into beautiful single-piece maps, where range, character traits, and terrain interact in deeply intricate tactical layers.

Lead your companions, raise your favorite characters, and experience battles unfolding across an unknown continent — alongside a story that probes the very foundation of the world itself.

DIGITRE:SUM 10/20 is a fast math action puzzle where you link adjacent numbers to total 10 or 20 and clear them from the board.

At first, even spotting a combination that totals 10 can be difficult. But with every attempt, combinations begin to emerge from what once looked like scattered numbers. Soon, 10s and 20s jump out at you—and careful calculation gives way to instinctive action.

Play again and again to chase SCORE and cut CLEAR TIME. Simple rules, the thrill of chasing records, and the spirit of classic arcade puzzle games—all through numbers.

ARCADE


Clear numbers one after another on a board that rises from below. Advance through the LEVELs and aim for ALL CLEAR before the blocks reach the top.

A higher SCORE, a shorter CLEAR TIME, a better rank. Keep playing and beat your own records.

Build CHAINs with consecutive clears to boost your score. Keep clearing glowing TARGET blocks to grow your TARGET STREAK for even more points. When enabled, BURST clears blocks across the board to help you escape a tight spot.

VS


Clear TARGETs to send attacks that push up your opponent’s board. Build CHAINs and TARGET STREAKs for bigger attacks and force your opponent toward the top.

Your own attacks can cancel incoming attacks while they are pending. Once an attack activates, it can no longer be cancelled, so timing matters. If you cannot lower your board within three seconds at the top, you lose. Choose when to attack and when to defend to win.

PUZZLE


Make 10 or 20 on a fixed board with no rising blocks, and remove every number to solve the puzzle. Think ahead about how the remaining blocks will fall and set up your next move.

Two challenges test your speed and endurance on a rising board. Choose between cutting your time and pushing your score higher.

  • BLITZ — Race to make 50 clears of 10 or 20. Spot each combination quickly and beat your best clear time.
  • ENDLESS — A score attack with no finish line. The board rises faster as your LEVEL increases. Keep clearing until GAME OVER and aim for the highest score you can.

ONE SCREEN. TWO ARMIES. ONE FRONT.

Real-time strategy, plus an auto battler cup. One match, a few minutes.

The screen is split in two. Thousands of DOTS hold one half, thousands of PIXELS hold the other. Where they meet is the front. You do not select units: you paint. Paint a spot and your army gets denser there. The denser side pushes the front. Push it across the whole screen and you win.

PAINT YOUR FLOW.

  • Left button: thicken your army where you paint.
  • Right button: thin it out and send the troops elsewhere.
  • Your army is not infinite: every strong spot leaves a weak one.
  • Hold more ground, get more reinforcements.

SPHERES FLOW. SQUARES JUMP.

  • DOTS pour into valleys and arrive like a wave. They have to travel.
  • PIXELS hold the high ground and jump across the screen with the scan heads.
  • Pick your side, or let the coin toss decide. Two armies, two ways to play.

BOMB. FREEZE. ERASE.

  • The bomb: a fuse, then a hole in their army.
  • The freeze: everything in the circle stops moving and stops getting help.
  • The mega eraser: hold, drag, wipe them out.
  • The ground: dig trenches for your dots, raise ridges for your pixels.
  • Attacks cost energy. It refills while you fight.

SET THE BOARD. PRESS PLAY.

  • Your board: 2 rows by 8 lanes on your edge, like a chessboard.
  • 5 pieces: PAWN spawns, RAM pushes, MORTAR shells, VACUUM erases, FREEZER freezes.
  • Each piece fights in its own lane. Pair them for combos: FEED and SALVO.
  • A cup of 8: quarter-final, semi-final, final. Best of 3 rounds of 40 seconds.
  • Between rounds: take 1 piece out of 3, or refuse and the next hits harder, up to x5.
  • 8 generals, each with a signature machine. Knock one out to find theirs.

THREE LOOKS. ONE KEY.

  • GLOW: neon armies in the dark.
  • SPHERES VS VOXELS: the battlefield in relief.
  • RETRO: the whole war inside a 1995 paint program.

THE BRIEFING.

  • Solo: against the computer. 3 difficulty levels: easy, normal, hard.
  • 1v1: against a friend on your local network (LAN).
  • Watch: let two computers fight and steal their tricks.
  • Auto cup: solo, 8 generals, 5 pieces, a new bracket every cup.
  • Sound: every effect is synthesized by the game. The notes climb as you conquer.
  • Safe mode: no flashes, no screen shake. Offered at launch.
  • Windows. Mouse and keyboard. Interface in English.

DAEMON DOORS is a build-crafting roguelike set in a corrupted digital system. You climb through floors, challenging minions and the guardians of each firewall.

How to play

* Choose doors by color. Each room offers doors of different colors (red, green, blue, golden, purple). The color influences what can appear and feeds your progress in that color.
* Resolve what is on the other side. Turn-based combat, gold chests, keys, potions, sacrificial altars, bargaining goblins, blood fountains, traps, and special events.
* On each floor, a shop followed by Rooms. Equip your stones well to survive them all.
* It is a roguelike, so death = end of the run.

Build your run with Stones and Spells:

* Stones (perks): passive effects that stack — more ATK, lifesteal, shields by color, counterattack, thorns, chain damage, gold economy, and dozens of others. Slots are limited, so every choice matters.
* Spells: strong effects that alter your run and combo with the stones.
* Cursed Stones: debuffs from unfinished missions. (YOU CAN BUILD YOUR RUN BY GAINING THIS)
* Color XP: In some runs, opening doors of the same color grants permanent bonuses to ATK, DEF, and max HP. Specializing in one color or diversifying is the challenge of the run.

Missions and Firewall Guardians

Each segment brings a contract with an objective, a reward for completing it, and a penalty for failing. At the end of each segment, a Firewall Guardian awaits. Each Guardian has its own trick — extorting crystals, all doors locked, freezing your attack, shutting down your Stones — and the final Guardians reserve the cruelest challenges.

In summary

* Genre: Build-crafting roguelike / roguelite, turn-based combat.
* Session: quick runs.
* For fans of: players who enjoy risk-based decisions, build synergies, and mastering a system run after run.

DaiDee 大弟 is a single-player roguelike built on Hong Kong Big Two combo grammar. No opponents, no passing, no AI opponents. The puzzle is you versus your own hand and the round's score target.

How it plays

  • Each round you draw 16 cards, keep 13, and split them into legal Big Two combos: singles, pairs, triples, straights, flushes, full houses, bombs all within a strict play budget.

  • Play order matters. Climbing Ladders and seizing the table with bombs builds Flow, the multiplier on your score. Round score = Power × Flow, minus penalties for unplayed cards.

  • 2s are your finishers. Play a group of 2s right after another combo to Link (+Flow), or close the round on a 2 Finisher for a bonus and the 2♠, the single highest card in the deck, is always waiting for the right moment.

Progression and difficulty

  • Between rounds, spend money on Style cards that rewrite how your hand can be split: turn a triple plus a stray card into a Cracked Bomb, substitute a rank in a straight, or fold two pairs into one four-card play.

  • Bosses impose constraints, reversed ladders, a Tax Collector, a seat reserved for your highest card. Miss the target and the run ends.

Features

  • True Hong Kong Big Two grammar: straights, flushes, full houses, bombs, 2 Links, finishers

  • Runs built on partitioning and ordering, no opponents, no dead draws

  • Style cards across grammar, scoring, sequencing, economy, and manipulation

  • Escalating targets and boss constraints
